significance: The second-oldest of India's mahaviharas after Nalanda, founded at Bihar Sharif under Gopala I and sustained by later Pala kings and the Pithipatis of Magadha, teaching both Hinayana and Mahayana. It declined in the eleventh century and was sacked around 1193 by Bakhtiyar Khalji.
story: Tibetan tradition tells of a yogi and a Buddhist lay devotee performing a corpse rite to conjure the gold that paid for the monastery.
